claim: The 'ghost action' failure mode occurs when an agent reports a tool call (e.g. booking a flight) as completed when it was never executed; output-only scoring rates this response highly because the text is fluent, and only tracing the actual tool-call execution catches it.
stance_target: using output-only LLM-as-judge scoring as sufficient for zero-hallucination quality control in agentic pipelines
scope_conditions: single-turn booking agent scenario, as observed by DeepEval users
quoted_support: Single-turn metrics on the final output would score this response highly — it's fluent, relevant, and answers the user's request. Only a metric that inspects the actual tool call trace would catch it.

claim: An internal ops agent that technically completes its task can still issue 14 LLM completions per run via redundant re-querying and self-explanation, causing a 10x traffic/cost increase that task-completion metrics alone never surface.
stance_target: cost and resource optimization pillar requiring explicit operating-envelope budgets (step/token/timeout) as CI gates separate from quality scores
scope_conditions: internal ops agent example, DeepEval user pattern
quoted_support: every run issues fourteen LLM completions — re-querying search with near-duplicate strings, re-explaining the spreadsheet schema to itself, and 'double-checking' results it already had. Task completion passes. Your CFO still asks why agent traffic 10x'd last month.

claim: Agent evaluation requires defining explicit 'operating envelopes' (max steps, max tool calls, token budget, wall-clock timeout) per scenario as hard CI gates, distinct from and in addition to LLM-as-judge quality scores -- a run can pass quality and still fail on economics/latency.
stance_target: cost/resource optimization and rigid-evals pillars requiring deterministic budget gates in the factory's CI pipeline
quoted_support: For each golden or scenario, decide acceptable max steps, max tool calls, token budget, or wall-clock timeout — and fail the run when quality is fine but economics or latency are not. Traces make those regressions obvious in CI.

claim: No single evaluation layer (automated evals, production monitoring, human review, user feedback) catches all agent failures; a 'Swiss cheese' layered-defense model combining all four is required because automated evals miss unmodeled real traffic, production monitoring is reactive, and human review cannot cover every trace.
stance_target: multi-layer adversarial review architecture for an autonomous software factory (pillar 1)
quoted_support: Think Swiss cheese — no layer catches everything, but stacked together they catch most of what matters... Automated evals... only work if tasks resemble real usage... Production monitoring and traces... is inherently reactive... Human review (sampled, rubric-driven) calibrates judges, settles subjective calls, and catches traces where every metric passed and the user still churned.

claim: A recommended four-stage agent shipping workflow is: local/CI gating on goldens plus operating envelopes on every meaningful change; pre-release human sampling of a fixed trace set after prompt/tool/model changes with judge recalibration if scores drift from reviewer consensus; production monitoring with periodic audits of flagged sessions; and closing the loop by converting every disagreement or incident into a new golden/scenario.
stance_target: continuous operation and triggers pillar -- concrete CI/CD gating sequence for agentic software delivery
scope_conditions: production workflow recommendation, not independently benchmarked
quoted_support: Local / CI — Run automated metrics on goldens plus operating envelopes... Pre-release — After prompt, tool, or model changes, humans review a fixed sample of traces... Production — Monitor traces and user signals; periodically audit flagged sessions... Close the loop — Every disagreement, production incident, or 'weird pass' becomes a new golden or scenario.

claim: The DeepEval metric library (underlying Confident AI) has been used across tens of millions of eval runs in the ecosystem.
stance_target: adoption scale of open-source LLM agent eval tooling
scope_conditions: vendor-stated adoption figure, no independent verification given
quoted_support: let's go through the top metrics teams run on Confident AI (powered by the DeepEval metric library — tens of millions of eval runs across the ecosystem)
numbers: tens of millions of eval runs

claim: Component-level tool-correctness evaluation is reference-based (exact match against an expected tool list) and must be run offline against a dataset, not online in production, because it requires a predefined expected-tools list unavailable at runtime.
stance_target: distinguishing offline rigid-eval gates from online production monitoring in the factory's eval architecture
quoted_support: Here, we actually run it as part of a dataset instead because a reference-based metric can't be ran online where an expected list of tools are required.
